Data handling

Privacy Policy

Use this page to understand how guest information is handled in the booking and route-delivery process. The standard should be narrow, purpose-bound, and tied directly to the route being operated.

Collection

Only route-relevant guest data should be collected

Names, contacts, passenger lists, and health-screening details should exist to run the route safely and lawfully, not to build a marketing profile.

Use

Data exists to operate the booking

Guest data is used for permits, screening, rooming, route coordination, and communication tied directly to the confirmed booking.

Protection

Access should stay narrow and purpose-bound

Only the teams or institutions that need the information for execution or compliance should receive it.

Operational use

Booking data should stay tied to route delivery

The practical reason for collecting guest information is to execute private routes safely and in compliance with local access or screening requirements.

  • Permit and ticket handling requires accurate passenger information.
  • Ijen-related routes may require health-screening records and verification.
  • Pickup, rooming, and route communication depend on reliable contact details.

Disclosure boundary

Sharing is limited to operational and regulatory need

Where data must be shared, it should be shared with the bodies or partners directly involved in route execution, compliance, or medical handling.

  • Official access or permit authorities when required.
  • Medical or screening partners for Ijen-related route handling.
  • Internal operational staff coordinating the confirmed booking.

Guest rights

Questions about data handling should not be buried

Guests should be able to ask how their information is used and what part of the booking process requires it.

If a booking is not proceeding, data handling should still remain proportionate to what was actually required for inquiry support and regulatory processing.
